**EU CBAM Supplier Partnership Strategy — 2026 Full-Financial Phase**  
*Co-Governed Emissions Compliance for European Buyers Sourcing Steel & Aluminum from India, Türkiye, and North Africa*

---

### Executive Thesis: “Co-Own the Carbon Before the Certificate”
The EU’s full CBAM phase (Regulation (EU) 2023/956, Art. 5–16) transforms embedded emissions from a reporting exercise into a verified, priced import liability. For a European industrial buyer, the 2026 risk is no longer only €65–€95+/tCO₂e price exposure; it is **relationship rupture**—suppliers interpreting CBAM as disguised protectionism, withdrawing offtake, or failing verification, which triggers customs/ACD suspension, supply interruption, and carbon-leakage migration to lower-standard markets.

This proposal replaces “buyer audits supplier” with a **shared emissions-governance model**: co-created data architecture, tiered technical rescue, differentiated material-route contracts, realistic accreditation timelines, EU-aligned verification, and an explicitly **commercial—not diplomatic—stakeholder dialogue** protected by de-risk clauses.

---

### 1. The 2026 Regulatory Reality — What Changes at the Border

| Dimension | Transitional Phase (Oct 2023 – Dec 2025) | Full Financial Phase (2026 Onward) |
|---|---|---|
| **Legal basis** | Quarterly self-declarations only | **Art. 5–16**: Authorized CBAM Declarant (ACD) status; embedded-emissions declarations; quarterly reports; **annual declaration; certificate surrender**; 5-year audit trail |
| **Verification** | Self-declared acceptable | **Mandatory third-party verification** (ISO 14065 / ISO 14064-3) by EU-accredited or mutual-recognition body; report **<12 months at import**; **actual metered data preferred**; **EU implementing-regulation default emission factors used as audited fallback** where metered data is unavailable |
| **Data / Registry** | Manual CBAM reports | **EU CBAM Registry schema**; **buyer’s ACD team submits declarations via EU portal**; supplier / shared platform provides **validated data package only**—**no direct supplier write access to the EU registry** |
| **Cost** | Zero direct cost | Buyer / importer pays **EU ETS-linked price** for verified Scope 1 (direct) + Scope 2 (indirect—**required for aluminum**) via CBAM certificates; penalties under Art. 16 (up to €50–€100 per unreported tonne / Member State fines) apply; **customs suspension / denial of import clearance is a separate ACD/compliance-status risk**, not an automatic Art. 16 fine |
| **Material differentiation** | Not specified | **Primary aluminum (~6–11 tCO₂e/t)** vs. **secondary/recycled (~0.5–1.5 tCO₂e/t)**; **blast-furnace / BOF steel (~1.5–2.5 tCO₂e/t)** vs. **EAF / scrap (~0.3–1.0 tCO₂e/t)**. Contracts must specify route category because cost profiles diverge 4–6× |
| **Perception / fairness** | Administrative burden rising | **Protectionism grievance intensified**; EU producers retain declining free allowances; developing-economy suppliers face cost without equivalent EU climate finance; **exit / carbon-leakage risk is acute for low-margin primary smelters** |

**Implication:** If suppliers exit, verification collapses, or the buyer’s ACD compliance is breached, the buyer faces supply interruption, **customs/ACD suspension**, regulatory denial, and liquidity shock.

---

### 2. The Six Partnership Pillars — Co-Owned Governance

| Pillar | Function | Corrected / Deepened Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| **P1. Joint CBAM Governance & Data Sovereignty** | Co-create emissions data; shared digital pipeline; supplier retains ownership | **Pre-filing pipeline for buyer’s ACD only**; GDPR tiered roles (granular = supplier controller; aggregated ACD filing = buyer controller); accreditation timelines (18–36 mo for new local accreditation) honored by using EU/mutual-recognition bodies immediately |
| **P2. Tiered Technical Activation** | Objective readiness assessment; embedded assistance; protect supplier confidentiality | **Objective entry criteria** with **supplier-consent financial assessment (NDA / third-party review)**; Track 3 rescue uses consent-protected criteria (not direct audited demands); **transitional-period quarterly reports (Oct 2023–Dec 2025) serve as the baseline** for 2026 verification |
| **P3. Shared Carbon-Cost & Procurement Architecture** | Quantified cost-sharing, shadow-price forecasting, transition finance, material-route modeling | **Route-specific clauses** (primary/secondary Al; BF/EAF steel); contracts include **EUR currency and governing-law provisions**; **price-band triggers**; **buyer procurement-mix shift** toward EAF / recycled Al as an immediate exposure-reduction lever |
| **P4. Perception Management & Equitable Framing** | Co-authored dialogue; EU climate-finance / technology-transfer advocacy; diplomatic de-risk | **Named trade bodies** (ISA, TCUD, SAD, Euro-Med federations); **EU-India FTA / retaliation de-risk clause**; dialogue is **industrial upgrade, not unilateral policy endorsement**; supplier neutrality protected |
| **P5. Regulatory Integration & Verification Ecosystem** | Accredited verifiers; EU registry integration; buyer legal compliance; **default-factor alignment** | Per-region accreditation pathways (**NABCB / TÜRKAK / EU MLA**); **EU default emission factors referenced**; ACD filing checklist; verification uses metered data with defaults as audited fallback |
| **P6. Shared Competitiveness, Leakage Contingency & Procurement Mix** | Joint “CBAM-Ready” certification; co-invested decarbonization; **low-carbon sourcing shift**; quantitative migration contingency | **Quantified migration contingency** (20% projected offtake / 24 months / € cap); **regional sourcing co-investment** if supplier migrates; low-carbon procurement premiums for EAF / recycled Al |

---

### 3. Supplier Profile Mapping — Region, Readiness, Grievance & Route

| Region / Cluster | Technical Readiness | Perception / Fairness Grievance | Dominant Emission Pathway | Partnership Tailoring |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **India — Steel / Al** | Medium–High (integrated); Low (SMEs). Coal-heavy grid drives high indirect. | **High protectionism suspicion**; EU-India FTA context raises government-retaliation risk; framing as EU market-capture attempt. | **Steel:** BF / DRI direct dominates; EAF / scrap cuts embedded carbon 60–70%. **Alum:** Indirect dominates; **primary (~6–11)** vs. **secondary (~0.5–1.5)**. | Cluster verification hubs; **route-specific shadow-pricing caps**; green-H₂ / scrap co-investment; renewable PPA co-investment; dialogue via **ISA / AAI**; **diplomatic de-risk clause** |
| **Türkiye — Steel / Al** | Medium (Customs Union aids literacy; indirect tracking weak; aluminum indirect high). | Mixed — some fairness due to EU integration; others see cost-push without compensation. | **Steel:** EAF / DRI mix improving. **Alum:** High indirect from grid; renewable PPA feasible. | Customs-Union-aligned fast-track (**TÜRKAK / ISO 14065**); shared digital reporting; **phased 50/70/100% cost split**; solar / green-H₂ co-investment; dialogue via **TCUD / SAD** |
| **North Africa — Morocco / Algeria / Tunisia / Egypt** | Low–Medium. Morocco renewable advantage; others fossil-heavy; verification sparse; primary smelters fragile. | **Strong fairness grievance**; perceived as EU imposing costs while EU producers retain subsidies; **high exit / migration-to-non-EU risk** for low-margin primary smelters. | **Steel:** Direct dominant; Morocco green-electricity potential. **Alum:** Morocco renewable lowers indirect if PPA secured; Algeria/Egypt fossil-heavy; **primary smelters face severe cost**; secondary lower. | **Capacity-first activation** (buyer funds EU-accredited verification immediately); co-fund **local accreditation (18–36 mo)**; renewable-transition co-investment; explicit fairness messaging with **Euro-Mediterranean federations**; **Track 3 rescue with consent-protected review**; **quantified migration contingency** |

---

### 4. Technical Architecture — The Shared Data Pipeline (Corrected for Registry Access & Sovereignty)

**Joint Digital Hub (Cloud-Based Supplier-Data Vault)**
- **Standard:** ISO 27001 / SOC 2 Type II; EU-hosted (GDPR) with regional mirror nodes; **EU CBAM Registry-compliant XML/JSON** schema.
- **Data Format:** GHG Protocol Corporate Standard (Scope 1, 2, 3 upstream where relevant); **EN 15935** alignment; embedded-emissions declarations structured per **Art. 5 Reg 2023/956**.
- **Audit Trail:** Immutable / WORM / blockchain-audited storage for verification reports, revisions, approvals; **5-year retention** per Art. 16.
- **Accreditation Integration:** All verification reports uploaded with verifier accreditation number, accreditation body, ISO 14065 / 14064-3 reference, digital signature, and report date (<12 months at import).

**The Corrected Pipeline — No Direct Supplier Registry Submission**
- **Hub function:** Data formatting, schema validation, emission-factor consistency checking (against EU default factors where needed), and verifier-accreditation matching.
- **Output:** A **validated declaration package** delivered to the **buyer’s Authorized CBAM Declarant (ACD) team**.
- **ACD action:** The buyer’s ACD submits declarations personally via the **EU CBAM Registry portal / customs IT interface**; **only the designated ACD has registry write access**.
- **Supplier access:** Supplier has **read access to aggregated reporting** and **write access only to their granular data vault**; no direct submission rights.

**GDPR / Data Sovereignty — Tiered by Purpose (Corrected)**
- **Granular production-level GHG data:** Supplier is **controller / data owner**; platform is **processor** under supplier instructions; buyer does **not** process for purposes other than aggregated filing without separate consent.
- **Aggregated import-declaration tier** (product-category totals for ACD filing): Buyer is **controller** for compliance filing; platform is **processor**; supplier provides via **Article 28 DPA with tier-specific instructions**.
- **Explicit prohibition:** Buyer may not unilaterally publish supplier-level granular emissions or use them for non-CBAM commercial negotiation without supplier consent.

**Accreditation Pathways — Realistic Timelines**
- **EU / Universal:** EU ETS accredited verifiers listed on EU CBAM / EU ETS registry.
- **India:** **NABCB** under EU MLA / ILAC-MRA; Indian bodies partner with EU-accredited auditors for immediate CBAM acceptance; long-term local accreditation pursued in parallel.
- **Türkiye:** **TÜRKAK** mutual recognition; TÜRKAK-accredited bodies serve immediately.
- **North Africa:** **Morocco (COFRAC / EU MLA)** for accredited bodies; **Algeria / Tunisia / Egypt** rely on **EU-accredited verifiers deployed locally** (immediate Q1 2026); buyer co-funds long-term local accreditation (Year 2–3). **Verification does not wait for new accreditation.**

---

### 5. Tiered Technical Activation — The 3-Track Model (Objective, Consent-Protected, Rescue-Enabled)

| Track | Mandatory Entry Criteria (Auditable) | Activation Package | Timeline | Rescue / Termination Protocol |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Track 1: Verified Ready** | Existing GHG inventory (ISO 14064 / GHG Protocol); verified report <12 mo; ISO 14001 / 14064-1 cert; production >50 kt/yr steel or >20 kt/yr Al; audit readiness ≥8/10; EU-compatible data system. | Fast-track; CBAM clause active; co-invest in marginal efficiency. | Q1 2026 | 60-day embedded remediation if verification fails; no termination without support. |
| **Track 2: Assisted Verification** | Partial GHG data; no accredited verification; audit readiness 4–7/10; production >10 kt/yr; internal inventory exists; direct + energy data available with engineering support. | Buyer-funded embedded team (3–6 mo sprint): inventory build, **EU-accredited / mutual-recognition verifier selection**, EU format training, hub onboarding; buyer pays **60% verification + consulting cost**; **local accreditation not required to start**. | Q1–Q2 2026 | If verification fails by Q3, automatic Track 3; no punitive termination. |
| **Track 3: Foundational / Rescue** | **Objective rescue criteria:** production <10 kt/yr **OR** debt/equity >0.7 **OR** operating loss 2+ quarters **OR** audit readiness <4/10 **OR** no GHG inventory; **CBAM cost >3% COGS**; verification cost >€15k relative to revenue; high indirect emissions with no renewable access. | Buyer-funded verification setup + transition finance (**min 60% cost**); supplier contributes 40% via staff/data or deferred repayment; **12-month Bridge Contract** at 120% volume with full CBAM cost absorption + technical team. | Q1 2026 – Q4 2026 | **90-day support required before any termination**; if supplier signals exit, activate Bridge Contract; if exit persists after 12 mo, buyer co-invests in migration to lower-carbon process or relocates sourcing within region. **Financial assessment uses supplier consent / NDA / third-party review; direct audited financial demands prohibited.** |

**CBAM Readiness Score (0–10):** GHG inventory completeness (2) + verification status (2) + data-system compatibility (2) + audit readiness (2) + balance-sheet stress / capital access (2). **Score <4 = Track 3; 4–7 = Track 2; ≥8 = Track 1.**

**Leveraging Transitional Reports:** The Oct 2023–Dec 2025 quarterly CBAM reports—though approximate—are the only historical embedded-emissions baseline. Suppliers must upload them to the hub at onboarding. Buyer and verifier use them to construct preliminary inventories, identify high-emission suppliers for Track 3 priority, calibrate shadow-price forecasts, and establish 2026 baselines (verified data will correct approximations).

---

### 6. Shared Carbon-Cost Architecture — Contract Design, Routes & Liquidity

**Example Contract Amendment — “CBAM Adjustment Mechanism”**

> *“(a) Definitions. ‘CBAM Certificate Price’ = monthly average EU ETS spot/futures price (€/tCO₂e) per EEX / Ember / CBAM registry; ‘Embedded Emissions’ = verified direct (Scope 1) + indirect (Scope 2) per tonne, per **Art. 5 Reg 2023/956**, by **Product Route** specified in Annex A. (b) Cost Pass-Through Cap. Year 1 (2026): Supplier may pass through up to **50%** of (CBAM Price × Embedded Emissions); Buyer absorbs 50%. Year 2 (2027): cap **70%** if Decarbonization Milestones met; if missed, 6-month grace. Year 4 (2029): cap **100%** if Supplier achieves ≥20% verified embedded-emissions reduction from **2026 baseline** (calibrated using transitional reports + verified data); otherwise Buyer retains **15% co-share**. (c) Price-Band Trigger. If CBAM Certificate Price exceeds **€100/tCO₂e** for 2 consecutive months, Parties convene Joint Council within 15 days to renegotiate sharing and activate Transition Finance Facility. (d) Shadow-Price Budgeting / Route-Specific Reserves. Buyer budgets internal carbon reserve at **€85/tCO₂e** (2026 baseline) + 15% volatility; **Primary Al reserve uses 6–11 tCO₂e/t**; **Secondary Al reserve uses 0.5–1.5 tCO₂e/t**; **EAF steel ~0.3–1.0 tCO₂e/t** vs. **BF/BOF steel ~1.5–2.5 tCO₂e/t**. Supplier receives 30-day advance notice of estimated CBAM invoice based on verified declarations. (e) Verification Timing. Supplier submits verified declarations **45 calendar days prior to intended import** to allow ACD readiness, certificate procurement, and customs filing; **actual EU customs entry declaration occurs at border per national customs timelines**, not 45 days in advance. (f) Governing Law & Dispute Resolution. This Agreement governed by **[English / Swiss / buyer jurisdiction] law**; disputes resolved by **ICC arbitration**, seat [neutral / buyer jurisdiction], language English, confidential proceedings. (g) Currency Risk. All CBAM cost calculations are in **EUR**. If supplier contract is denominated in non-EUR currency (INR, TRY, MAD, EGP), price-band adjustments and pass-through calculations shall use **ECB monthly average EUR rates** to prevent supplier margin erosion from EUR fluctuation; buyer may offer EUR-denominated sub-contract or hedging support.”*

**Material Route Sub-Clauses (Differentiated Architecture)**

| Material / Route | Emissions Profile | Co-Investment Architecture | Contract Milestone |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Steel — BF / BOF / DRI** | **Scope 1 direct** dominates (~1.5–2.5 tCO₂e/t); EU defaults apply if metered data unavailable | Co-invest in **scrap-metal recycling**, **green-hydrogen DRI retrofit**, carbon-capture at source; buyer provides 30–50% capital for 3-year offtake at carbon-adjusted price | Direct Reduction Milestone: Increase scrap-based EAF share ≥15pp or green-H₂ substitution ≥10% by Year 3; failure = 6-month grace with technical support |
| **Steel — EAF / Secondary** | Low direct (~0.3–1.0 tCO₂e/t) | Buyer increases procurement share as **low-carbon pathway**; co-invest in scrap supply security | Low-Carbon Premium: Buyer pays modest green premium for certified EAF supply, reducing total CBAM exposure |
| **Aluminum — Primary Smelting** | **Scope 2 indirect dominates** (~6–11 tCO₂e/t); EU indirect reference factors apply if metered data unavailable | Co-invest in **renewable PPA / solar / hydro** for electrolysis electricity; indirect reduction is primary CBAM lever | Renewable Power Purchase & Indirect Cap: ≥50% renewable electricity by Year 2, ≥80% by Year 4; verified indirect emissions fall ≥25% from 2026 baseline by Year 4; transition finance tranches tied to PPA execution |
| **Aluminum — Secondary / Recycled** | Very low (~0.5–1.5 tCO₂e/t) | Buyer shifts procurement mix; co-invest in scrap/recycling infrastructure | Low-Carbon Procurement Premium: Buyer prioritizes secondary supply; supplier receives transition finance for recycling capacity |

**Buyer Liquidity & Reserve (Illustrative, Route-Adjusted)**
- **Primary Al:** 50 kt × 8.5 tCO₂e/t (median) × €75 = €31.9M/yr
- **Secondary Al:** 50 kt × 1.0 × €75 = €3.75M/yr
- **EAF Steel:** 200 kt × 0.7 × €75 = €10.5M/yr
- **BF/BOF Steel:** 200 kt × 2.0 × €75 = €30M/yr
- **Year 1 Shared (50/50):** Budget at **€97.75/t** (with 15% volatility); 90-day liquidity reserve ≈ €13–€32M depending on mix.
- **Shadow-Price Forecast Band:** €65 / €85 / €110.

**Transition Finance Facility (Annex B)**
Buyer establishes €10–€15M regional fund (co-capitalized with supplier contributions / EU climate-finance access) for verification, renewable/scrap infrastructure, and Bridge Contract funding. **Condition:** Recipient commits to verified emissions-reduction milestones, 3-year supply contract, and route-specific targets (primary → renewable; BF → EAF / scrap).

---

### 7. Perception Management, Equity & Stakeholder Dialogue — Industrial Upgrade, Not Unilateral Endorsement

**Named Dialogue Partners & Bodies**
- **India:** Indian Steel Association (ISA); Aluminum Association of India (AAI); DGFT / Ministry of Commerce; EU Delegation to India.
- **Türkiye:** Federation of Turkish Steel Producers (TCUD); Aluminum Producers Association (SAD); TÜRKAK; EU Delegation / Customs Union Joint Committee.
- **North Africa:** Euro-Mediterranean industrial federations (EuroChambers / MEDEF / COMECE); national associations; EU Delegation / ENI / EIB climate-finance window.
- **EU / Global:** DG TAXUD; DG CLIMA; EIB; EU CBAM Expert Group.

**Dialogue Protocol**
1. **Quarterly Joint CBAM Council:** Buyer + regional trade body + accredited verifier + chamber; agenda: verification progress, cost-sharing, price-band updates, accreditation timelines.
2. **Semi-Annual EU Delegation / DG TAXUD Engagement:** Buyer and supplier representatives **co-present** fairness / technology-transfer papers to DG TAXUD / DG CLIMA, emphasizing **mutual recognition, EU climate-finance access for developing economies**, and **development-sensitive implementation**.
3. **Industrial-Upgrade Framing:** All co-authored materials emphasize **technical upgrading, supply security, and joint competitiveness**—not supplier endorsement of EU carbon policy.

**Diplomatic De-Risk Clause — EU-India FTA / Retaliation Context (Corrected)**
- Dialogue is **commercial / industrial**, not diplomatic endorsement of EU climate policy.
- Suppliers maintaining **public neutrality** are protected by agreement.
- Buyer must **not publicly attribute supplier cooperation to government-level endorsement**.
- If Indian government retaliation risk emerges (tariffs, regulatory scrutiny on cooperative exporters), dialogue shifts to **purely technical verification cooperation** without joint public statements; buyer provides legal / diplomatic support to supplier.
- Co-authored statements include explicit language: *“This dialogue addresses industrial compliance and mutual competitiveness; it does not constitute endorsement of any government climate-policy position by participating suppliers or their governments.”*

**Equity Safeguards**
- Supplier veto over granular-data use; aggregated declarations only for ACD filing.
- Verification cost shared proportionally (buyer 60% Track 2 / 60% Track 3; supplier 40% via staff/data/deferred repayment).
- Bridge Contract guarantees 90-day support before any termination.

---

### 8. Implementation Roadmap — 2026 Activation

| Quarter | Action | Key Deliverable |
|---|---|---|
| **Q1 2026** | Onboarding; transitional report upload; readiness scoring (0–10); Track 3 rescue activation; ACD registration; contract amendments executed | Regional Joint Councils formed; Track 2/3 supplier lists; ACD status confirmed |
| **Q2 2026** | Verification sprints for Track 2; EU-accredited verifiers deployed (India NABCB / Türkiye TÜRKAK / North Africa EU bodies); hub onboarding; first price-band monitoring | First verified data packages; 45-day pre-submission pipeline tested |
| **Q3 2026** | First verified declarations submitted by ACD; customs filing practice; Joint Council reviews cost-sharing; transition finance disbursed for PPA / scrap / H₂ projects | First quarterly CBAM declarations filed; migration contingency baseline set |
| **Q4 2026** | Milestone review (direct reduction / renewable % / recycled-share targets); accreditation progress check for local bodies; shadow-price forecast update; 2027 contract renegotiation if price-band triggered | Verified 2026 baselines established; co-invested decarbonization projects operational; supplier retention rate measured |

---

### Conclusion

This strategy treats CBAM not as a barrier to be audited away, but as a **shared industrial upgrade** that preserves supply relationships by co-owning data, co-funding verification, co-sharing cost, co-investing in low-carbon routes (EAF steel; recycled aluminum; renewable-powered primary aluminum), and defending suppliers from both regulatory failure and diplomatic retaliation. The buyer’s ACD submits to the EU registry; suppliers own their granular data; contracts specify EUR terms, governing law, material routes, and price-band triggers; and rescue protocols ensure no supplier is abandoned because of carbon-cost shock.

**The objective is not procurement extraction—it is verified, shared competitiveness.**

### 4. Technical Architecture — The Shared Data Pipeline (Corrected for Registry Access, MWh, Audit Trail, Calendar)

**Joint Digital Hub (Cloud-Based Supplier-Data Vault)**
- **Standard:** ISO 27001 / SOC 2 Type II; EU-hosted (GDPR) with regional mirror nodes; **EU CBAM Registry-compliant XML/JSON** schema.
- **Data Format:** GHG Protocol Corporate Standard (Scope 1, 2, 3 upstream where relevant); **EN 15935** alignment; embedded-emissions declarations structured per **Art. 5 Reg 2023/956**.
- **Audit Trail:** **WORM / immutable storage with qualified digital signatures (eIDAS / EU trust services where available)**; 5-year retention per Art. 16; digital audit logs; **no blockchain overhead required** for SME accessibility.
- **Accreditation Integration:** All verification reports uploaded with verifier accreditation number, accreditation body, ISO 14065 / 14064-3 reference, digital signature, report date (<12 months at import).

**The Corrected Pipeline — No Direct Supplier Registry Submission**
- **Hub function:** Data formatting, schema validation, emission-factor consistency checking (actual vs. EU default factors; MWh consumption validation for aluminum), and verifier-accreditation matching.
- **Output:** A **validated declaration package** delivered to the **buyer’s Authorized CBAM Declarant (ACD) team**.
- **ACD action:** The buyer’s ACD submits declarations personally via the **EU CBAM Registry portal / customs IT interface**; **only the designated ACD has registry write access**.
- **Supplier access:** Supplier has **read access to aggregated reporting** and **write access only to their granular data vault**; no direct submission rights.

**GDPR / Data Sovereignty — Tiered by Purpose**
- **Granular production-level GHG / MWh data:** Supplier is **controller / data owner**; platform is **processor** under supplier instructions; buyer does **not** determine purposes/means for granular processing (unless separate data-sharing agreement exists).
- **Aggregated import-declaration tier** (product-category totals for ACD filing): Buyer is **controller** for compliance filing; platform is **processor**; supplier provides via **Article 28 DPA with tier-specific instructions**.
- **Explicit prohibition:** Buyer may not unilaterally publish supplier-level granular emissions or use them for non-CBAM commercial negotiation without supplier consent.

**Accreditation Pathways — Realistic Timelines**
- **EU / Universal:** EU ETS accredited verifiers listed on EU CBAM / EU ETS registry.
- **India:** **NABCB** under EU MLA / ILAC-MRA; Indian bodies partner with EU-accredited auditors for immediate CBAM acceptance; long-term local accreditation pursued in parallel.
- **Türkiye:** **TÜRKAK** mutual recognition; TÜRKAK-accredited bodies serve immediately.
- **North Africa:** **Morocco (COFRAC / EU MLA)** for accredited bodies; **Algeria / Tunisia / Egypt** rely on **EU-accredited verifiers deployed by buyer** (immediate Q1 2026); **buyer co-funds long-term local accreditation** (Year 2–3). Verification does not wait for new accreditation; buyer pays deployment costs.

**Aluminum Indirect (Scope 2) — Metrology & Factor Documentation (New Precision)**
- **Metering:** Supplier shall measure and record actual electricity consumption in **MWh per production line / per tonne of aluminum** using utility invoices, certified sub-meters, or production-line energy management systems.
- **Factor Source Documentation:** For each reporting period, supplier must provide:
  1. **Actual MWh** by source (grid, on-site renewable, purchased PPA);
  2. **Emission factor source:** EU implementing-regulation reference / national grid average / or **contractual renewable factor** supported by **Guarantee of Origin (GO), REGO, I-REC, or equivalent**; if contractual renewable is used, the supplier must retain PPA/contract and GO documentation for verifier review;
  3. **Separation:** Direct process emissions (Scope 1) and indirect electricity emissions (Scope 2) reported separately; indirect dominates primary smelting (~70–85% of total) and must be verified independently.
- **Verification:** Verifier reviews MWh evidence against utility/production records and confirms factor-source consistency; EU default indirect reference factors used only as audited fallback where metered MWh is unavailable and properly justified.

**Annual Calendar & Reporting Deadlines (New Specificity)**
- **Quarterly supplier forecasting reports:** Due within **45 days of quarter-end** (April 15, July 15, Oct 15, Jan 15) to enable forecasting and verification scheduling.
- **Supplier final verified data to buyer/ACD:** **April 30** of following year.
- **Buyer ACD annual declaration & certificate surrender:** **May 31** of following year for imports in preceding calendar year (e.g., May 31, 2027 for 2026 imports).
- **Customs entry:** Actual customs declaration at border per national timelines; 45-day pre-submission is for ACD readiness, not customs filing.

### 6. Shared Carbon-Cost Architecture — Contract Design, Routes, MWh, Calendar & Anti-Retaliation

**Example Contract Amendment — “CBAM Adjustment, Verification, Calendar, and Non-Endorsement Mechanism”**

> *“(a) Definitions. ‘CBAM Certificate Price’ = monthly average EU ETS spot/futures price (€/tCO₂e) per EEX / Ember / CBAM registry; ‘Embedded Emissions’ = verified direct (Scope 1) + indirect (Scope 2, **metered MWh**) per tonne, per **Art. 5 Reg 2023/956**, by **Product Route** specified in Annex A; ‘MWh Evidence’ = metered electricity consumption records with factor-source documentation per implementing regulation. (b) Aluminum Indirect Verification Obligation. For Primary Aluminum, Supplier shall provide **monthly MWh consumption by production line / per tonne**, sub-meter or utility-invoice evidence, and emission-factor source documentation (EU reference grid factor or contractual renewable with GO/REGO/I-REC); indirect emissions are calculated separately from direct process emissions and reported with MWh evidence. (c) Cost Pass-Through Cap. Year 1 (2026): Supplier may pass through up to **50%** of (CBAM Price × Embedded Emissions); Buyer absorbs 50%. Year 2 (2027): cap **70%** if Decarbonization Milestones met; if missed, 6-month grace. Year 4 (2029): cap **100%** if Supplier achieves ≥20% verified embedded-emissions reduction from **2026 baseline** (calibrated using transitional reports + verified MWh/direct data); otherwise Buyer retains **15% co-share**. (d) Price-Band Trigger. If CBAM Certificate Price exceeds **€100/tCO₂e** for 2 consecutive months, Parties convene Joint Council within 15 days to renegotiate sharing and activate Transition Finance Facility. (e) Shadow-Price Budgeting / Route-Specific Reserves. Buyer budgets internal carbon reserve at **€85/tCO₂e** (2026 baseline) + 15% volatility; **Primary Al reserve uses 6–11 tCO₂e/t**; **Secondary Al reserve uses 0.5–1.5 tCO₂e/t**; **EAF steel ~0.3–1.0** vs **BF/BOF ~1.5–2.5**. Supplier receives 30-day advance notice of estimated CBAM invoice. (f) Verification Timing & Calendar. Supplier submits verified declarations to Buyer/ACD by **April 30** for annual filing; Buyer’s ACD files annual declaration and surrenders certificates by **May 31** of following year; interim quarterly forecasting reports due within **45 days of quarter-end**; actual EU customs entry declaration at border per national timelines, not 45 days in advance. (g) Governing Law & Dispute Resolution. This Agreement governed by **[English / Swiss / buyer jurisdiction] law**; disputes resolved by **ICC arbitration**, seat [neutral / buyer jurisdiction], language English, confidential proceedings. (h) Currency Risk. All CBAM cost calculations in **EUR**; if supplier contract denominated in non-EUR currency, adjustments use **ECB monthly average EUR rates**; buyer may offer EUR-denominated sub-contract or hedging support. (i) No Endorsement / Anti-Retaliation Protection. Supplier’s cooperation with verification, data sharing, and hub onboarding under this Agreement **does not constitute endorsement, approval, or alignment with any EU climate policy, government position, or diplomatic stance by Supplier, Supplier’s affiliates, or Supplier’s government**. Nothing herein shall be construed as Supplier endorsing CBAM as fair, protective, or climate-effective, and Buyer shall not publicly or contractually attribute Supplier’s compliance to government-level endorsement. Supplier retains sole discretion over public statements regarding EU trade policy; if government retaliation risk emerges, dialogue shifts to purely technical cooperation with neutral public framing, and Buyer shall provide legal/diplomatic support to Supplier.”*
